title: Assessment of Critical Quality Attributes of a GMP-Manufactured ADSC-Based ATMP During Hypothermic Storage
content: The short-term stability of cell-based advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs) is a critical factor in their clinical handling and applicability. This study evaluates a multiparametric stability assessment approach using a GMP-manufactured ADSC-based ATMP as a model product. It consists of an ADSC suspension in Ringer’s lactate contained in polypropylene syringes. The in-use stability of the ADSC-based ATMP was evaluated over 36 h of hypothermic storage (2-8°C). Ten GMP-manufactured batches derived from a single qualified donor were analyzed immediately after preparation (T0) and after storage (T36) using validated methods for viability, sterility, mycoplasma status, endotoxin level assessment, and macroscopic appearance evaluation. Additionally, complementary quality tests using flow cytometry were applied. Cell integrity was characterized by Annexin V-FITC/7-AAD staining, whereas FSC/SSC analysis, doublet discrimination, and qualitative re-adhesion testing were used to investigate cell aggregation and post-storage recovery capacity. All tested parameters remained within predefined acceptance criteria at both time points. Mean cell viability decreased from 95.1 ± 1.8% to 88.2 ± 2.8% but remained above the acceptance threshold (≥70%) in all batches. Sterility, absence of mycoplasma, endotoxin levels, and suspension appearance met specifications. Flow cytometry demonstrated preserved membrane integrity, a small proportion of early apoptotic cells, and no changes in cell-size distribution or aggregation. These findings indicate that the investigated ADSC suspension maintains viability, structural integrity, and microbiological quality during short-term hypothermic storage under clinically relevant conditions. The study highlights the utility of complementary flow cytometry-based methods for stability assessment of fresh ATMPs.
